what_this_proves: The thirteen secret patterns are now applied where output actually leaves the process, not only on the security agent's own write paths. The production database password no longer comes back from /v1/world/facts, no log line carries a credential, and the one endpoint that answers without an owner session cannot quote a DSN.

red_first.method: The four changed files were copied to a backup with sha256 digests, reverted to HEAD one surface at a time, the suite re-run, and restored by digest verification (sha256sum -c: 4/4 OK).
red_first.world_model_and_health: 5 failed / 12 passed - the snapshot carried the DSN password, the dependency fact was the raw setting, an arbitrary fact and an uncertainty detail both leaked, and the health check error quoted the credential.
red_first.log_pipeline: 5 failed / 12 passed with `redact_secrets` neutered to a pass-through - the DSN, a password-named key, a nested authorization header, a traceback, and the pattern naming all went through in clear text.
red_first.why_it_matters: Without this the tests would only show that the new code agrees with itself.

surfaces.world_model: Redaction sits on `_Collector.fact` and `_Collector.uncertain` - the door every section writes through - rather than on the one collector that leaked, so a section added later is covered without remembering to be. `strip_uri_credentials` removes the userinfo BEFORE the redactor sees it, so the fact still reads postgresql+asyncpg://***@10.0.0.5:5432/pagentos and still answers the question it exists for.
surfaces.logs: `redact_secrets` is a structlog processor placed immediately before the renderer and after format_exc_info (a traceback is the likeliest place a DSN appears, and it is only a string by then). `SecretRedactingFilter` covers the standard-library pipeline, attached to the root HANDLERS - a filter on a logger is not consulted for records propagating up from a child, which is exactly what uvicorn's and SQLAlchemy's records are.
surfaces.health: Both the per-check error string and the assembled `checks` map. The map-level pass exists because the endpoint aggregates ~18 independently-written health_check() methods, each of which claims to carry no secrets and none of which was checked.

two_rules_not_one: A key whose NAME means credential has its string value replaced outright; every other string is pattern-scanned. Both apply at every depth. No pattern can recognise `hunter2` - only the key says what it is - and scanning only the top level of an event would miss {"body": {"password": ...}}, which is the shape a log event almost always has.
deliberate_non_redactions: `tokens: 1430` from an LLM call matches the key vocabulary and stays an integer: only string values are replaced by key name. Redaction that eats the observability it protects costs more than it saves.

Trace ids, sha256 digests and commit shas pass through untouched - a bare long hex string is deliberately not a pattern (app/security/redaction.py says why: it would make the redactor mangle its own audit trail).
A health failure carrying no secret is reported verbatim; most health errors are the operator's only clue.
one_vocabulary: Patterns come from app.memory.policy (M8's own list already reads them from there); credential-shaped key names come from app.research.forbidden_keys, the token list the browser worker and the Cloud Core already agree on. A pattern added to either shows up on all three surfaces, and this pipeline cannot drift into a fourth opinion about what a credential looks like.
found_on_the_way: `redact_value` applies patterns recursively but NOT the key-name rule, so the first version of the processor let {"body": {"password": "hunter2"}} through in clear text. The log processor now walks the tree itself.

structlog is not this process's only writer: uvicorn's access lines and SQLAlchemy's engine logging go through the standard library, past the processor chain entirely. Requirement 683 says no secret is logged, not no secret is logged by our own code.
measured_not_guessed: The redaction costs under 1% on a representative subset (10.25s without the processor, 10.34s with it, same four suites, same process). The first full-gate run took 776s against a 694s baseline; measuring the processor in and out of the chain showed that difference was run-to-run variance, not this change.
proof: PROVEN_AUTOMATED for all five. PROVEN_REAL needs a production release (roadmap decision 0, owner-gated): the production check is that /v1/world/facts comes back with no credential in it and that a deliberately failed health probe names the failure without the DSN.
stated_bounds: SecretRedactingFilter is attached to the handlers that exist when configure_logging runs - the single stream handler basicConfig installs. A handler added afterwards does not inherit it.
The key-name rule replaces string values only. A credential stored as a non-string (bytes are covered; a custom object is not) is not caught by the key rule, only by the patterns once it is rendered.
